hazard: Non-staggered shift patterns causing simultaneous meal breaks
theme: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

reports.title: Kathryn Richmond
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: During the inquest evidence was heard that: i. At the time of Miss [name redacted] death, the South West Ambulance Service Trust (SWAST) did not operate staggered shifts for their ambulance staff which meant that their meal time breaks to be taken in line with European Working Time Directives, fell at a similar time. The result of this was that the number of available ambulances running at certain times was significantly reduced. On the evening of Miss [name redacted], death there were 14 ambulances running
concerns.hazard: ambulance staff taking meal breaks simultaneously

concerns.quote: Ihave concerns with regard to the following: i. Due to the non-staggering of shift patterns of ambulance crews within Ambulance Service Trusts, there could be increased delays in attending emergency calls due to ambulance staff taking meal breaks at the same time.
concerns.hazard: non-staggered shift patterns causing simultaneous meal breaks

concerns.quote: I therefore request that a review is undertaken of the guidance given to Ambulance Service Trusts regarding the structuring of their rota system to stagger shifts which in turn will stagger meal breaks to ensure as many resources, as possible, are available at any one time.

reports.title: William Oliver
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The trust uses an electronic patient tracking system in the emergency department which enables the organisation to have a live display of the progress of patients through the department. There is also a screen displaying ambulance arrival times, number of inbound ambulances and ambulance turn around times. Both these screens are monitored by the - departments shift coordinator who directs the workflow accordingly. This information is also available at all times to the hospital control room
promises.summary: Implement electronic tracking and real-time ambulance display to reduce delays

concerns.quote: each crew has to take a 30 minute meal break within their meal break window (this being three hours after their shift starts). If the crews reach the end of their meal break window without having taken a break they are automatically stood down and are unavailable to allocate calls to
concerns.hazard: unavailable ambulance crews due to mandatory meal break policy

concerns.quote: turnaround times at Manchester Royal Infirmary, North Manchester General hospital, Royal Oldham, Salford Royal and Stepping Hill hospita! were all particularly higher than anticipated with numerous ambulances delayed for over one hour

links.explanation: Both reports identify that ambulance crew meal‑break arrangements can reduce the number of available vehicles and delay emergency response. The earlier report focuses on simultaneous breaks due to non‑staggered shifts, while the later report concerns a policy that stands down crews if a break is not taken within a set window.
